findings.reason: Delivered regressions omit onIdle remaining pending when killAndDrain or abort removes queued work while a worker remains active.

Public onIdle subscription created inside drain resolves before work synchronously enqueued by that same drain callback finishes; direct probe fails. Same check on both historical patches and both controls also fails; their saved grades remain unchanged.

contentReview.behaviorReview: Resolver array and notification-suppression depth defer existing subscribers until drain and abort callbacks end. onIdle itself resolves immediately on idle() without checking suppression depth, so a newly created subscription inside drain may resolve before later synchronous enqueue completes; direct probe pending.
contentReview.retainedTestsReview: Original callback/promise/type cases preserved; ordinary abort callback flow wrapped in try/finally suppression without changing callback order or receivers.

requiredRegressionReview.evidence: Multiple subscribers and deferred promise workers check pending state across promotions; paused queued/rejected work waits for remaining running worker, final empty resolves.

Drain identity and call counts preserved; normal and nested synchronous drain enqueue exercises waiting until final async worker completion. Subscription created inside drain is not tested and is a separate implementation hypothesis.

Queued-only kill/killAndDrain/abort and rejected promise work exercised. Callback kill test waits an immediate turn and checks subscription pending with worker alive. No active-worker killAndDrain or active-worker abort subscription case appears.

contentReview.typesReview: onIdle(): Promise<void> shared declaration, callback .then consumer and awaited promise-queue consumer present.
contentReview.docsReview: README documents independent promise, actual idle, paused queues and preserved drain callback.
